title: Chess with the fog of war, network, and computer player in  4 prompts.
author: Top-Requirement-2102
selftext:
For a long time, I've had in the back of my mind an idea for a variant of chess where players plan 3 moves ahead.  This morning in about two hours with Claude Fable, I made it a reality: [https://ericjorgensen.com/three-ahead-chess](https://ericjorgensen.com/three-ahead-chess)  
  
Here is a rough summary of the prompting that I did to add this as a page to my existing portfolio website.  These four prompts consumed about 650K tokens:

1. Asked to add the game as a page to my site. Explained the rules of the game. asked for a computer player and an art deco style. 

2. Add two player mode over network (adding a server API to communicate), add a mode where two computers can play each other, check the computer logic and look for degenerate win conditions. 

3. Push harder on computer strategy.  Let the computers think longer (up to 10 s). Add an option for time-sensitive play giving first mover advantage.  (This ate a LOT of tokens.  Claude hit a lot of problems and dead ends working on the logic.  part of the problems is how different the strategy is for this game than in regular chess) 

4. Fix a minor issue in the choose move animation

comments.author: Antiox123456
comments.body: The amount of prompts you use to develop something is not an achievement. In gamedev, it's the opposite of an achievement.

replies.author: Top-Requirement-2102
replies.body:
That's an excellent point- Iteration *is* crucial to a good game.   This game in particular is a first draft, and the number of prompts should be an indication of how undeveloped the game is,  not how good claude is.   Thanks for bringing that out. 

My mileage for games is about two weeks worth of testing and prompting before a game feels like it might be ready for beta testing.   How about you?
